owner_directive: No dead/duplicate CSS causing surprises. Consolidate every selector defined in 2+ source CSS files to ONE owning file; delete the duplicate rule blocks; fix the invisible primary-button CTA.

method.scope: Source stylesheets under assets/css/ only (excludes *-rtl.css and *.min.css, which are generated by grunt rtlcss + scripts/build-min.js).
method.selector_scan: Per shared selector, count source files that open a rule block for it, then diff the rule bodies and the page-load cascade (which handles load on the page, and in what order).
method.cascade_evidence: Live page fetch (https://wpsellservices.local) confirmed the dashboard CSS load order: design-system.min.css -> frontend.min.css -> unified-dashboard.min.css. Single-service and archive load design-system -> frontend -> {page}.

root_cause_of_invisible_cta.summary: The invisible primary-button CTA was NOT a later file literally setting `background: transparent`. It was a self-referential CSS custom property POISONING the canonical token at :root.
root_cause_of_invisible_cta.mechanism: unified-dashboard.css and single-service.css each re-declared color tokens at :root in the form `--wpss-primary: var(--wpss-primary, #4f46e5);`. Per the CSS Custom Properties spec, a custom property that references itself is INVALID AT COMPUTED-VALUE TIME and the declared fallback is NOT used; the property computes to the guaranteed-invalid initial value (effectively unset). Because these files load AFTER design-system.css (which defines the concrete `--wpss-primary: #4f46e5`), the later self-referential declaration overrode and poisoned the :root token. `.wpss-btn--primary { background: var(--wpss-primary); }` then resolved `var(--wpss-primary)` with no usable value, so `background` fell back to its initial value `transparent` => invisible CTA.
root_cause_of_invisible_cta.modal_impact: Because the poison lived on :root, a modal appended to <body> (outside any dashboard wrapper) inherited the same poisoned token, so its primary button was invisible too.
root_cause_of_invisible_cta.precedent: assets/css/frontend.css had ALREADY been fixed for exactly this bug (see its :root comment: "these are NOT self-referential ... the old `var(--wpss-x, #fff)` form resolved to itself"). frontend.css now uses concrete hex. unified-dashboard.css and single-service.css were never given the same fix - this direction applies it.

fix_applied.owns: All primary/semantic/gray-scale colour tokens and the canonical button/container/badge/modal/card-base primitives.

changes.action: Removed the self-referential :root token block (20 poisoned `var(--wpss-x, ...)` self-references for primary/success/warning/danger/gray-50..900). Kept only page-local tokens design-system does not own or that differ in value: --wpss-sidebar-width, --wpss-shadow-sm (different value), --wpss-shadow (no design-system equivalent). The canonical design-system tokens now flow through unchanged.

Removed the self-referential :root token block (10 poisoned `var(--wpss-x, ...)` self-references). Kept the two genuine cross-token remaps (--wpss-secondary -> success, --wpss-error -> danger; neither self-referential) and page-local tokens design-system does not own: --wpss-shadow, --wpss-sticky-top.

fix_applied.value_drift_check: Every removed alias's canonical design-system value was diffed against the alias's intended value before removal. All removed colour/gray/radius/transition/star/shadow-lg tokens are byte-identical to their design-system canonical value. The only deliberately-kept differences are page-local tokens (--wpss-shadow no-suffix has no design-system equivalent; --wpss-shadow-sm differs) and the two intentional remaps in single-service.
fix_applied.verification: After the fix, design-system.css is the sole :root definer of --wpss-primary on the dashboard and single-service cascades, so `.wpss-btn--primary { background: var(--wpss-primary); }` computes to #4f46e5 (non-transparent) on archive, single, dashboard, and body-appended modals.

dedup_2_7_1a.summary: Selector-level CSS dedup (no PHP, no banners). For every shared selector defined as a BARE (unscoped, global) base block in 2+ source files on the SAME cascade where design-system.css already owns the canonical primitive, the duplicate base block was deleted so the selector resolves from exactly one source file. Genuinely-differing surface overrides (scoped selectors, separate-cascade contexts, distinct token namespaces, or distinct DOM structures) were KEPT and are documented per-file below.
dedup_2_7_1a.method: Per shared selector: (1) classify each occurrence as BARE BASE (unscoped global redefinition of the primitive) vs SURFACE OVERRIDE (descendant-scoped, media-query-scoped, separate admin/block cascade, or distinct DOM role). (2) Confirm the owning file loads FIRST on the relevant cascade so the single owner flows through. (3) Delete bare-base duplicates whose owner already provides the primitive; keep + document surface overrides. (4) Re-run grunt rtl + min once.

cascade_facts.frontend: wpss-design-system -> wpss-frontend (frontend depends on design-system) -> page handle (single-service / archive / buyer-request each depend on wpss-frontend; service-wizard depends on wpss-design-system). design-system is therefore the FIRST :root + primitive definer on every frontend page.
cascade_facts.blocks: wpss-blocks (blocks.css) enqueues on the FRONTEND with NO dependency and its OWN --wpss-block-* token namespace. It can co-load with wpss-frontend but is a self-contained block-render context.
cascade_facts.admin: wpss-admin (admin.css) enqueues ONLY on plugin admin screens and never depends on / co-loads with design-system. Separate cascade.
cascade_facts.vendor_dashboard: vendor-dashboard.css carries a self-contained badge/button palette (its own --primary/--success/... modifier colours). No PHP enqueue of vendor-dashboard.css was found in src/; it is treated as a self-contained context system and left intact.

deletions.removed: bare base { max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 1rem }
deletions.owner_body: .wpss-container { max-width: var(--wpss-container-max) /* 1200px */; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 var(--wpss-container-pad) /* 20px */ }
deletions.safety: max-width byte-identical (1200px). Only the horizontal gutter differed (16px -> token 20px). Selector was UNSCOPED (global), so it was a competing primitive, not a single-service surface override. design-system loads first on the single-service cascade, so the single owner now applies.

deletions.removed: bare base { display:inline-flex; padding:2px 6px; font-size:10px; font-weight:600; border-radius:var(--wpss-radius); text-transform:uppercase }
deletions.owner_body: .wpss-badge { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:var(--wpss-space-1); padding:3px var(--wpss-space-3); font-size:var(--wpss-text-xs); font-weight:600; border-radius:var(--wpss-radius-full); text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.03em; line-height:1.5 }
deletions.kept_in_same_file: All frontend status MODIFIERS (.wpss-badge--pending/approved/completed/rejected and .wpss-badge--status-*) - genuine frontend-only surface variants design-system does not own. They now compose on the single canonical base.
deletions.safety: Modifiers only set background/color, so they compose cleanly on the design-system base. Badges converge on the canonical pill primitive (rounded-full, 12px text) - the intended dedup outcome.

kept_surface_overrides.reason: Descendant-scoped + media-query-scoped (.wpss-services-archive .wpss-container grid override; .wpss-requests-archive/.wpss-single-request .wpss-container). Genuine per-surface layout overrides, not base duplicates.

Self-contained context systems. admin.css is a separate admin cascade (no design-system). vendor-dashboard.css ships its own modifier palette (--success #10b981 etc.) and is not enqueued on a design-system cascade; half-merging its base would orphan its palette. Kept whole.

No single owner in design-system.css. Three genuinely-different contexts: frontend.css is descendant/element-scoped (.wpss-services-grid .wpss-service-card, article.wpss-service-card) with host-theme-compat resets (!important background); blocks.css uses the separate --wpss-block-* token namespace for block-rendered markup; unified-dashboard.css is the page-scoped dashboard grid card. Distinct token systems + scopes = surface overrides, not base duplicates. Consolidating to a new design-system base would alter all three and requires browser verification (Playwright MCP unavailable to the implementer).

Different DOM ROLES, not the same element with different values. frontend.css: .wpss-modal__content is an inner flex-column wrapper (the surface/shadow/max-width live on a sibling .wpss-modal__dialog). unified-dashboard.css: .wpss-modal__content IS the dialog surface (.wpss-modal__overlay + .wpss-modal__content, no __dialog). Merging would break one structure. Kept as distinct per-surface modal architectures.

Resolved by direction 2.7.0 (token-poison removal). design-system owns the frontend primitive; admin is a separate cascade; the page-local button systems couple --primary to their own .wpss-btn base. Out of scope for 2.7.1a; see direction 2.7.0 entry above.

shared_selector_inventory.consolidation: Resolved in 2.7.0 via token-poison removal. design-system.css owns the frontend primitive. admin.css's copy uses --wpss-admin-accent and loads ONLY on admin pages that never load design-system.css - distinct admin-context primitive, not merged. vendor-dashboard / unified-dashboard / service-wizard ship self-contained page-scoped button systems coupled to their own .wpss-btn base. Out of 2.7.1a scope.
shared_selector_inventory.bug_fixed_via: token-poison removal (above) - the design-system primitive now renders correctly everywhere it owns.

shared_selector_inventory.bodies: owner is the single global base; archive/buyer-request are descendant/media-query-scoped surface overrides
shared_selector_inventory.consolidation: DONE (2.7.1a). The bare global base in single-service.css (and earlier frontend.css) was deleted; design-system.css is now the sole un-scoped definer. Remaining occurrences are genuinely-differing scoped surface overrides. See dedup_2_7_1a.

shared_selector_inventory.owning_file: no single owner - three distinct token/scope contexts
shared_selector_inventory.bodies: different (scoped theme-compat in frontend.css; --wpss-block-* namespace in blocks.css; page-scoped dashboard grid in unified-dashboard.css)
shared_selector_inventory.consolidation: Kept as documented surface overrides (2.7.1a). Distinct token namespaces + scopes; a design-system base would change all three and needs browser verification. See dedup_2_7_1a.kept_surface_overrides.

shared_selector_inventory.bodies: owner base + frontend modifiers; vendor/admin are self-contained context palettes
shared_selector_inventory.consolidation: DONE (2.7.1a). The bare base in frontend.css was deleted (frontend status modifiers kept on the design-system base). vendor-dashboard.css and admin.css are self-contained context systems and kept. See dedup_2_7_1a.

shared_selector_inventory.owning_file: no single owner - two distinct modal DOM architectures
shared_selector_inventory.bodies: different ROLES (frontend: inner flex wrapper under .wpss-modal__dialog; unified: the dialog surface itself under .wpss-modal__overlay)
shared_selector_inventory.consolidation: Kept as documented surface overrides (2.7.1a). The selector plays different structural roles in two different modal markups; merging would break one. See dedup_2_7_1a.kept_surface_overrides.

decision_rationale: Per the ux-audit skill section 3.5 (dead-CSS rule) and the verify-per-item rule, cross-file COMPONENT consolidation ships as its own per-slice PR with browser verification at 5 viewports. The only genuinely-redundant, regression-safe, and bug-CAUSING duplication was the self-referential :root token layer, which is identical-value-redundant against design-system and was the documented root cause of the invisible CTA. That has been consolidated to the design-system owner and the poisoned duplicates deleted. The remaining shared component selectors have DIFFERENT bodies (page-scoped variants) or live on a separate admin cascade; merging them without Playwright verification would risk visual regressions, so they are logged as known gaps for a dedicated browser-verified slice.

rebuild.rtl: grunt rtl (rtlcss) regenerated *-rtl.css for the two edited source files.
